fact: The case study says Botswana's health sector comprises numerous digital health systems that operate in isolation, constraining interoperability and limiting data exchange; dated by publication, no event date given.

The estimates record P28,934,000 appropriated for MoH Computerisation, and its notes cite the Committee of Supply speech describing a Health Information Exchange and a Client Registry keyed on the Omang or passport number as ready for deployment; dated by the fiscal-year start, 2026/27.

The Minister of Local Government told Parliament that the Patient Information Management System, Integrated Patient Management System, DHIS2 and E Pulse are active but not interfaced to permit data sharing across all health facilities.

The minister said an Electronic Medical Records system is being piloted in two districts and, with the Clinic Information Management System, will link to the Botswana Health Information Exchange supporting a Master Patient Index across public and private facilities.

The Ministry of Health's Committee of Supply speech reports the Health Information Exchange being implemented, with its Client Registry and Facilities Registry ready for deployment and further expansion planned next financial year.
